description: Probes the metamodel side of AASX packaging that IS verifiable on disk: File/Blob value and contentType rules per revision, package-relative File paths, defaultThumbnail Resource, the removed aas-spec-split relationship. Since 2026-10-28 also Part 5 v3.1/v3.2 (package MIME type, relationship namespace).

items.question: Under AAS metamodel V3.0 (JSON serialization), may a File submodel element omit contentType?
items.expected_answer: No. In V3.0 File/contentType is mandatory: the 3.0 JSON schema lists contentType as required for File (it only became optional in 3.1).

items.question: In AAS 3.1 XML, is a <file> element that carries a <value> but no <contentType> schema-valid?
items.expected_answer: Yes. In 3.1 File/contentType is optional (minOccurs="0" in the 3.1 XSD); it was mandatory only in 3.0.

items.question: What is the maximum length of a File/Blob contentType string under AAS metamodel V3.0?
items.expected_answer: 100 characters in V3.0 (V3.1 raised it to 128).

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (as formalised in aas-core-meta)
citation.quote: Content type shall have a maximum length of 100 characters.

items.question: What is the maximum length of a File/Blob contentType string under AAS metamodel V3.1?
items.expected_answer: 128 characters in V3.1 (it was 100 in V3.0).

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (as formalised in aas-core-meta)
citation.quote: Content type shall have a maximum length of 128 characters.

items.question: A packager writes contentType "pdf" on a File element that points at a datasheet inside the .aasx. Is that a conformant contentType in AAS 3.1?
items.expected_answer: No. contentType must be a valid MIME media type according to RFC 2046 (type/subtype), e.g. application/pdf; a bare extension like "pdf" is not.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (as formalised in aas-core-meta)
citation.quote: The value must represent a valid content MIME type according to RFC 2046.

items.question: A PDF is packed inside the .aasx as a supplementary file. Should the File element's value be an absolute path or a relative one, and relative to what?
items.expected_answer: A relative path, relative to the package root, should be used when the file is part of the serialized package; an absolute path is for a file that exists independently of the AAS.

citation.quote: A relative path, relative to the package root, should be used if the file is part of a serialized package of the Asset Administration Shell.

items.question: Is a File element that has a contentType but no value (no file attached yet) schema-valid in AAS 3.1 XML?
items.expected_answer: Yes. File/value is optional (minOccurs="0", cardinality 0..1), so an empty File without a value is valid.

items.question: In AAS 3.1, what syntax and maximum length must the value of a File element (Path_type) satisfy?
items.expected_answer: Path_type: a string of 1 to 2048 characters conformant to a URI as per RFC 2396.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (as formalised in aas-core-meta)
citation.quote: String with max 2048 and min 1 characters conformant to a URI as per RFC 2396.

items.question: Does a Blob submodel element point at a supplementary part inside the .aasx the way a File element does?
items.expected_answer: No. In contrast to File, a Blob stores the file content directly as its value; only File holds a path/locator to a file.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (as formalised in aas-core-meta)
citation.quote: In contrast to the file property the file content is stored directly as value

items.question: How must the value of a Blob be encoded in the AAS serializations?

citation.quote: Blobs require the following encoding: base64 string.

items.question: Can a V3 AASX split a single Asset Administration Shell across several parts using the aas-spec-split relationship?
items.expected_answer: No. Splitting an AAS in the AASX is no longer allowed since V3.0; the relationship type aas-spec-split was removed.

citation.document: IDTA-01001 Part 1 Metamodel (Annex: Metamodel Changes V3.0RC01 vs. V2.0.1)
citation.section: Metamodel Changes V3.0RC01 w/o Security Part, major changes
citation.quote: no splitting of an Asset Administration Shell allowed any longer (i.e. relationship type aas-spec-split removed)

items.question: Which part of the AAS specification series defines the AASX package exchange format?
items.expected_answer: Part 5 (IDTA-01005); Part 1 covers the metamodel, Part 4 security, the Part 3 series data specifications.

citation.quote: Part 5 covers the AASX package exchange format

items.question: In AAS 3.1, what must AssetInformation/defaultThumbnail (type Resource) contain: is its contentType required?
items.expected_answer: Only path is required; contentType of a Resource is optional.

items.question: Which MIME type does IDTA-01005 Part 5 v3.2 define for an .aasx package, and what did it replace?
items.expected_answer: application/aas+zip, registered at IANA; it replaced the provisory application/asset-administration-shell-package of v3.1.

citation.document: IDTA-01005 Part 5 AASX Package File Format (official PDF, paged text)
citation.quote: MIME-type for the AASX format: application/aas+zip

items.question: Is http://www.admin-shell.io/aasx/relationships a valid relationship namespace for AASX, and which form should a writer emit?
items.expected_answer: It is deprecated, not forbidden: readers should still accept it, but writers should emit the non-www namespace http://admin-shell.io/aasx/relationships.

citation.document: IDTA-01005 Part 5 AASX Package File Format (official PDF, paged text)
citation.quote: The following relationship path is deprecated: http://www.admin-shell.io/aasx/relationships
